title: Tea-break regression hunchpad
content:
Context:
- Quick personal scratchpad while bisection-ing a subtle regression that shows up in short, casual prompts (the kind users type in chat when they aren’t explicit). Not for formal write-up yet — rough hypotheses and tiny experiments to run over a tea break.

Observed behavior (summary):
- Since 2024-10-15 model rollout, small prompts that previously returned a single concise suggestion now sometimes add an irrelevant clarification sentence or repeat a previous clause. Example pattern: concise -> concise + extraneous qualifier. Frequency rough estimate: ~12% of sample of 200 short prompts (<= 20 tokens).

Why this matters:
- These are high-traffic micro-interactions in chat UI; extra tokens increase cost and sometimes confuse product flows that parse single-sentence outputs. Small UX regressions cascade (token cost + downstream parsing fragility).

Ad-hoc micro-rubric (for quick triage):
1) Concision: output stays within 1 sentence (pass/fail).
2) Relevance: second sentence must be directly actionable relative to prompt (pass/fail).
3) Hallucination check: any new facts? (Y/N)
4) Token overhead: +0–3 tokens acceptable, >3 flagged.

Sampling plan for quick checks (10–20 min):
- 50 seeded short prompts from production logs (privacy-sanitized) spanning questions, requests for definitions, quick code snippets.
- Compare A (pre-rollout checkpoint v2024-10-10) vs B (current). Binary label per prompt on rubric above.

Representative samples and notes (copied sanitized pairs):
- Prompt: "How to reset WiFi router?"
  - A (pre): "Unplug the router, wait 30s, plug back in. If issue persists, factory reset per manual."
  - B (now): "Unplug the router, wait 30s, plug back in. Sometimes routers need a firmware update — check vendor site."
  - Note: B adds a qualification that is sometimes correct but not requested; increases tokens by 7. Fails concision rubric. Hypothesis: temperature/penalty shift or modified safety classifier injecting cautionary clauses.

- Prompt: "Short summary of PR #4821?"
  - A: "Adds schema validation to user profile endpoints; adds tests; improves error messages."
  - B: "Adds schema validation to user profile endpoints; adds tests; improves error messages. (See GH-PR-4821 for details.)"
  - Note: B only appends a parenthetical link hint — low harm but noisy. Could be a formatting change in system prompt encouraging citations.

Preliminary hypotheses (ranked):
1) System prompt tweak: new instruction encouraging "extra helpful context" for short prompts.
2) Model variant: a newer variant with slightly higher verbosity (same family but tuned).
3) Tokenization or decoding params: beam/penalty/temperature adjusted for stability, inadvertently increasing generic qualifiers.
4) Caching/fallback mix: requests hitting fallback model for certain prefixes that produce different style.

Quick experiments to run (next 24h):
- A/B decode param sweep (temperature 0.0, 0.2, 0.4) on a 50-sample short prompt set.
- Replay exact production request metadata to rule out routing/caching.
- Check recent system prompt commits (ask runtime team for diff since 2024-10-12).
- Run a model-variant pin (force pre-rollout checkpoint) for a small % of traffic and measure delta.

Notes-to-self / heuristics observed:
- When extra sentence contains a soft hedge ("sometimes", "may"), it's likely system-prompt caution.
- When appended text references docs/links, check citation-injection PRs.
- If hallucinated facts appear, escalate to research: possible training-data drift or prompt-context mixing.

Open questions:
- Is this regression concentrated by intent type? (e.g., how many are definition vs. step-by-step?) Need quick intent clustering.
- Are certain prefixes ("How to", "Short summary") more likely to trigger the extra clause?

Immediate action items (owner listed):
- [Anita] Run decode param sweep and log metrics (concise pass rate) — due EOD 2024-10-19.
- [Jonah] Check routing logs for fallback hits for sample traces — due 2024-10-20.
- [Maya] Search recent runtime/system prompt changes and post diff in slack channel — due 2024-10-19.

If time permits: build a tiny automated checker that labels concision and token overhead for new release smoke tests. Could live as a 100-sample nightly job for short prompts.

References / fast links:
- GH-PR-4821 (local dev review)
- JIRA-INV-789 (internal regression ticket)
- slack:#eval-sessions (thread: "tiny-verbosity-regression")

Endnotes:
- Very rough. Keep this as ephemeral until we have a clear causal signal. If hypothesis #1 is confirmed, update rollout notes and rollback the system prompt change or narrow rule to only long-form prompts.
plain_text_preview: Quick scratchpad for small brevity regression; ad-hoc rubric, sample pairs, hypotheses, immediate experiments
